newsitem.title: CHINA: China slams European Union for import restrictions.
newsitem.headline: China slams European Union for import restrictions.

text.p: China on Sunday criticised the European Union (EU) for imposing quota restrictions on Chinese imports and for launching anti-dumping investigations that could cost China billions of dollars.
The European Union should end its discriminatory and outdated practice of treating China as a non-market economy, the China Daily Business Weekly said.

"To guarantee a healthy development of the Sino-EU economic relationship, we wish the EU side could abandon its discriminatory treatment of China and treat Sino-EU economic links with a long-term viewpoint," it quoted Liu Youhou of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying.
Problems such as the EU's unilateral quota restrictions on Chinese goods were slowing the growth of trade between Beijing and Europe, Liu said.
The EU had recently stepped up anti-dumping investigations against Chinese imports, including important exports such as shoes, bags and unbleached cloth, he said.
If the investigations resulted in anti-dumping measures, Chinese losses could total several billion dollars, he said but gave no details.

It was difficult to respond to such anti-dumping suits because the EU treated China as a non-market economy and used statistics from other nations to estimate Chinese production costs, the newspaper quoted trade officials as saying.

Almost two decades of economic reform have introduced free-market mechanisms to China's centrally-planned economy, but economists say many state-owned manufacturers are still highly reliant on hidden subsidies such as loans from state banks.
Liu said changes to EU regulations that ended the tax-free status of many Chinese goods had also affected Chinese exports.

Chinese exports to the EU were worth $8.7 billion in the first half of 1996, down 0.3 percent compared with the same period the year before. Imports from the EU rose 4.4 percent to $9.0 billion, the China Daily Business Weekly said.
